dialect: Latin American Spanish (broadly neutral, ustedes for plural 'you')

profile.pronunciation_convention: IPA (Latin American, seseo); spoken = stress hint
profile.grammar_notes: Two copulas: ser (identity, origin, time, traits) and estar (location, current state). Existence with hay. Subject pronouns usually dropped; verb endings mark person. Politeness marked grammatically with tú vs usted (ustedes for all plural 'you' in Latin America). Negation with no before the verb; double negatives (no … nada/nunca). Questions by intonation or question words. Core modals/verbs: querer, poder, tener que, ir, venir, tener. Gustar-type verbs reverse the English subject (me gusta). Reflexive se, object pronouns lo/la/le before the conjugated verb. Periphrastic constructions: ir a + infinitive, estar + gerund, acabar de + infinitive, tener que + infinitive, volver a + infinitive. Past: preterite vs imperfect. Closed sets: subject pronouns, object pronouns, articles, question words, days of the week.
